claim: YouVersion announced Bible Loop on Nov 4, 2026 as the newest app in the YouVersion Family of Apps, created in partnership with OneHope, free.
quote: Bible Loop, the newest app in the YouVersion Family of Apps, gives teens a reason to slow down and spend more time in God's Word. Created in partnership with OneHope, the free app was built for teens at a stage of life when independence is growing and habits are forming.

claim: Per YouVersion, Bible Loop is available on Android and iOS in English, Spanish, Portuguese and French.
quote: Bible Loop is now available on Android and iOS in English, Spanish, Portuguese, and French.

claim: Features per YouVersion: verse memorization game with an anonymous leaderboard, Learning Loops (partner lessons, described in future tense), mood-matched Daily Check-Ins, Verse of the Day, Daily Prayers, 50+ Bible versions in 10 languages.
quote: Teens can start with a verse memorization game that turns daily Scripture into a habit, complete with an anonymous leaderboard for a little friendly competition. Learning Loops will add interactive lessons from partners teens love and trust, while Daily Check-Ins match devotional content to how a teen is feeling that day. A Verse of the Day and Daily Prayers round out the experience, with Bible text available in more than 50 versions across 10 languages.

claim: Bobby Gruenewald (YouVersion founder and CEO) said YouVersion created Bible Loop specifically for teens.
quote: teens are an important part of that vision, which is why we created Bible Loop specifically for them," said Bobby Gruenewald, founder and CEO of YouVersion.

claim: Rob Hoskins (OneHope co-founder and president) framed the app around preteens.
quote: We're meeting the next generation where they are, helping preteens engage meaningfully with God's Word and build habits that lay a foundation for a lifelong relationship with Jesus," said Rob Hoskins, co-founder and president of OneHope.

claim: The release cites a 2021 OneHope/Barna study: weekly Bible engagement reported by engaged Christian parents was 88% for ages 6-9 and 73% for ages 10-12 (parent-reported, engaged Christian families only).
quote: A 2021 OneHope study in partnership with Barna found that while 88% of engaged Christian parents of children ages 6-9 reported their children engaging with the Bible weekly, engagement dropped to 73% for children ages 10-12.

claim: The release cites a OneHope U.S. study that Gen Alpha spends an average of 4 hours 6 minutes online daily.
quote: In a recent U.S. study, OneHope found that Gen Alpha, whose oldest are now teens, spends an average of 4 hours and 6 minutes online daily.

claim: Barna published the Guiding Children study with OneHope in 2020 (not 2021), with Hoskins describing a dip in Bible engagement for 10-12-year-olds.
quote: This is clearly seen in our findings that show a substantial dip in Bible engagement for 10–12-year-olds.

claim: YouVersion's own Bible Loop page lists 995K+ installs across Android and iOS (first-party, not 1 million).
quote: 995K+ Installs across Android and iOS devices.

claim: Google Play shows Bible Loop at 1M+ downloads (Android only, Google's bucketed count), 4.3 stars.
quote: 1M+ Downloads

claim: faith.tools reports Bible Loop has been on Google Play since July 2024, i.e., well before the Nov 4, 2026 announcement.
quote: Bible Loop carries that same idea to teens, and it has been on Google Play since July 2024.

claim: App Store version history shows updates on Oct 28-29 adding French, Portuguese and Spanish and Learning Loops, just before the announcement.
quote: Now available in French, Portuguese, and Spanish!

claim: Store listings (not the release) describe streaks and crowns as part of the app.
quote: Level up your Streak as you read God’s Word

claim: The iOS listing advertises a leaderboard and personalized profiles.
quote: Create a personalized profile to track your journey and progress

claim: Apple App Store age rating for Bible Loop is 13+; Google Play rating is 3+.
quote: Age Rating 13+

claim: Google Play content rating is Rated for 3+.
quote: Rated for 3+

claim: Google Play Data safety (developer-declared): no data shared with third parties; collects device IDs, app interactions, optional approximate location, crash logs and diagnostics for analytics.
quote: The developer says this app doesn't share user data with other companies or organizations.

claim: Google Play Data safety says users cannot request deletion of data collected by Bible Loop.
quote: Data can’t be deleted The developer doesn’t provide a way for you to request that your data be deleted

claim: Apple privacy label (developer-declared, unverified by Apple): data collected is not linked to user identity (identifiers, usage data, user content).
quote: Data Not Linked to You The following data may be collected but it is not linked to your identity:

claim: YouVersion privacy policy (last modified Nov 16, 2025) covers Bible Loop and says no account is required to use YouVersion.
quote: You do not need to sign up for an account to use YouVersion.

claim: YouVersion privacy policy addresses minors generically via parental consent and supervision.
quote: You are solely responsible for providing supervision of the minor's use of YouVersion

claim: faith.tools says, citing YouVersion help, that Bible Loop has no account creation and stores streak/progress on device.
quote: No account is needed: YouVersion help says there is no account creation in Bible Loop, and a streak and progress are stored on the device itself.

claim: A CHI '26 study (Smith et al.), as summarized in a 2026 arXiv preprint, found a Bible app's gamified streak made some participants anxious or felt inauthentic.
quote: a gamified reading “streak” feature made some participants anxious and felt like an inauthentic way to track something as personal as scripture reading, and that the feature broke whenever a participant chose to read a physical Bible instead of the app

claim: The arXiv preprint authors caution designers about streak-style engagement features.
quote: designers should be wary of adding engagement-driving features, such as streaks, that could make users feel judged for reading scripture on paper or that treat scripture study as a metric to optimize rather than a personal practice.

claim: The same preprint notes apps focused on scripture content (short devotionals, Bible stories) saw their most-used features there.
quote: O’Leary et al. found that the most-used features of their church health app were the ones focused specifically on scripture, such as short devotional reflections and Bible stories

claim: Survey of 407 students found paper scriptures still frequently used, especially when seeking a spiritual experience.
quote: We found that paper scriptures are still frequently used even with the prevalence of technology, especially when the reader is seeking a spiritual experience.

claim: Teen user review on App Store says the app is a quick way to connect but physical Bible and own prayers are best.
quote: While reading the physical Bible and praying your own words are always best, this app is a great way to quickly connect with Him.

claim: Google Play reviewers asked for more translations and a login/friend feature.
quote: I was also curious as to why there isn't a personal login similiar to their Bible App.

claim: IMB and RevelationMedia plan an ASL animation of the Gospel of Luke, to be reanimated into other sign languages.
quote: This project … will be the world’s first, natural sign language animation of the Gospel of Luke in ASL,” RevelationMedia said in a press release.

claim: The often-cited '2% of deaf people reached' statistic has murky origins, per MinistryWatch.
quote: Only 2% of deaf people worldwide have been reached with the Gospel. The figure’s origin is murky, but it dates to at least 2019

claim: Deaf Missions completed what it describes as the first full ASL Bible in 2020.
quote: In 2020, Deaf Missions completed what it describes as the first full ASL Bible translation.

claim: Deaf Bible Society advertises its Deaf Bible app in 92 sign languages.
quote: as “available in 92 sign languages and growing every year,”

claim: Per YouVersion, the 30-Day Bible Challenge returns in November with a progress-tracking and friends feature; nearly 3 million signed up in 2025.
quote: nearly 3 million people worldwide signed up for the first year of the Challenge. This November, YouVersion hopes its community will build on that momentum, with the Challenge returning with a new feature that lets users track their progress and see how their friends are engaging alongside them.

claim: Per YouVersion, the 30-Day Bible Challenge invites daily engagement in print or app.
quote: At its heart is the 30-Day Bible Challenge, encouraging people to engage with God's Word every day during November, whether through a favorite print Bible or digitally through an app.
